subject: Request: TTFT / token-rate exception for streaming endpoints (Lighthouse Health)
messages:
From: Sam Elliott <sam.elliott@lighthouse.health>

Cc: devops@lighthouse.health
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming endpoint SLOs — request for exception

Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the streaming chat path looked promising for our clinician-facing assistant. As we scope the production contract there are a couple of SLO asks from our infra and compliance teams that we want to surface early so we can converge on a mutual action plan: 

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): for short-turn interactions (<= 256 context) we need TTFT around 250–350ms. For long-turn retrieval-assisted sessions (2k+ context, heavy KV warmups) our infra team is asking if Redwood can accept a narrower TTFT SLA or whether we should plan an explicit carveout.
- Sustained token throughput: when under steady-state load we need ~40 tokens/sec per connection for real-time UX; peak bursts sometimes hit 80 tokens/sec for short periods.

Our ask: can Redwood provide a written exception/waiver for TTFT for the streaming endpoints when model context or cache-warm conditions make the standard TTFT impractical? If an exception is possible, we’d like to see the proposed limits, any compensating commitments (fallback models, warm-up strategies), and an outline of how that would be reflected in the commercial docs (SLA attachment or playbook).

I’ve attached our SLO requirements and a short diagram of our integration. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

—Sam

Subject: Re: Streaming endpoint SLOs — request for exception

Hey all — technical view + concrete options below. I’ll keep it pragmatic so contracting can pick a lane.

Summary: streaming TTFT and sustained token/sec are orthogonal knobs. For short contexts (<512 tokens) we can confidently hit TTFT <= 350ms on our hosted fleet for the recommended model families. For long-context flows (>=2048 tokens) initial KV load + attention memory can push TTFT higher; in practice we see a wide distribution (350ms–1.2s) depending on model, quantization, and whether prefix caching exists. Sustained token/sec is primarily influenced by model throughput and our batching window — we can guarantee a sustained baseline but allow short bursts up to N for a limited duration.

Option A — No carveout (tight SLAs):
- TTFT <= 350ms for streaming (contexts <=512)
- Sustained token rate >= 40 tokens/sec; bursting to 80 tokens/sec for <=30s per minute
- Requirements on LH: provide steady pre-warm traffic (e.g., predictable concurrency profile) and single-region routing
- Pros: clean SLA, predictable for product. Cons: higher cost (dedicated warm pool) or limits on long-context flows.

Option B — Scoped exception (recommended for mixed workflows):
- TTFT SLA: <= 350ms for streaming when context <=512; for contexts >512 and <=2048 TTFT <=500ms; for contexts >2048 carveout: TTFT target 600ms with an allowance up to 1.2s for cold KV sessions
- Sustained token rate: baseline 35 tokens/sec; burst up to 80 tokens/sec but limited to 20% of connections overall in any 5-minute window
- Mitigations: prefix/KV caching, warm-pool reservation for peak windows (we can schedule warm windows), and automatic fallback to a lower-latency model variant (smaller quantized family) for the first chunk with subsequent hot-path using higher-quality model
- Commercial: this would be an SLA exception document (addendum) with an SLO appendix and a modest monthly credit schedule when TTFT exceeds the carved allowance more than X times per month

Option C — Non-streaming alternative (predictability-first):
- Recommend non-streaming (sync) endpoints for the heaviest long-context sessions: predictable latency (P95) and simpler billing profile
- TTFT not applicable; instead provide P95 completion latency guarantees and token/sec throttles

Requests from our side to finalize:
1) Can LH provide typical session length distribution (percentiles for context length and concurrency) so we can size warm pools?
2) Any hard regulatory need that prevents using fallback quantized variants for initial chunk?

If you want I can draft the exception addendum language (text + acceptance criteria + credit table) — I’ll include expected unit economics for warm-pool reservation vs. pay-as-you-go.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Aditya — this is helpful and maps to internal thinking. A few follow-ups from the platform side: 

- Session profile: ~70% of sessions are <512-context, ~20% are 512–2048, ~10% are >2048 (these come from long patient threads + retrieval). Peak concurrency expected 90 concurrent streams during working hours; average concurrency ~30.
- Regulatory: we cannot serve initial chunk with a model that does on-device PHI transformations without explicit validation; fallback quantized variants are ok as long as they run in the same private deployment and meet our security controls.
- Credits: if we accept the scoped exception (Option B) what is the baseline monthly credit schedule if TTFT exceeds carved allowances?

If you can pass a draft addendum with the credit table and warm-pool pricing we can route to procurement. We’re targeting a production start late July, so timeline is tight.

—Sam

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Elliott <sam.elliott@lighthouse.health>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming endpoint SLOs — request for exception

Sam — appreciated. We can commit to the recommended Option B carveout with the following commercial terms (high level) so procurement has something concrete: 

- Addendum: "Streaming TTFT & Token-Rate Exception — Lighthouse Health" attached as an SLA appendix.
- Credit table (monthly): if TTFT target for >2048 contexts exceeds allowance more than 10 times in a 30-day window, we will issue a service credit equal to 2% of that month’s Redwood usage for Lighthouse; if it exceeds 30 times, credit increases to 5%.
- Warm-pool pricing: reserved warm units priced at $X,XXX / unit / month (unit = n1.medium warm GPU slot); suggested initial reservation: 4 units for production ramp — Aditya can size precisely after LH usage profile confirmed.
- Security: fallback model variants must run inside the same private deployment (VPC) — we will validate the variant under LH security controls before activation.
- Next steps: 1) Aditya to deliver final addendum text by EOD Monday; 2) LH to share traffic percentiles (Aditya’s sizing input); 3) Monica to open a commercial redline in DocuSign/HubSpot for review.

I’ll attach the draft addendum and open a DocuSign when we have redlines. If that timeline works I’ll mark this as "SLA exception: draft" and Monica/Aditya will shepherd technical review.

—Monica
